Surah al-Mulk

It is also called Tabaraka, al-Māni'a (the Preventer), al-Wāqiya (the Protector), and al-Munjiya (the Deliverer). Al-Walī al-Malawī said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to love this surah because of the abundance of its knowledge, and he said: "I wish it were in the heart of every Muslim."

Its purpose is submission to God, because He is characterized by perfect dominion (al-mulk), which indicates complete power, which in turn indicates the definitive judgments of created things, which indicates complete knowledge, which indicates the judgments of made things; namely, knowledge of what is in the breasts, so that this knowledge necessarily results in the certainty of resurrection for the reckoning of servants according to their state of righteousness and obstinacy, as is the custom of kings in judging their subjects, so that wisdom may be perfected, blessing may be completed, and the surah of dominion may appear. Its name, al-Mulk, is clear in this, because dominion is the locus of submission for everyone who sees it. Likewise Tabaraka, because whoever is such has complete permanence and endurance, and has from every thing perfect submission and reverence. Likewise its names al-Māni'a, al-Wāqiya and al-Munjiya, because submission compels one to hold to the path of happiness; whoever holds to it is saved from what he fears, is prevented from every terror, and is protected from every creature. It also answers the question about who adheres to it, and this is among the most important matters. (In the name of God, before whose perfect greatness kings submit; the Most Merciful, whose blessing of origination encompasses all, and who clarifies the place of conduct; the Most Compassionate, who specially grants guidance to His friends and the removal of doubts.)

* *

When the previous surah concluded that whoever turns away from Him, He destroys, and no one can benefit him, and whoever turns toward Him, He elevates and chooses him, and no one can harm him, and it concluded that He strengthened Maryam, peace be upon her, until she reached the rank of perfection and granted her firm sincerity, and such a thing can only be done by one who has no equal, and one who has no equal is worthy that deeds be sincerely directed to Him and that one not turn to anything else in any state, because He is the King who possesses dominion, He said, stirring up the resolves toward insight, stirring up the will toward a discipline that yields all doors of happiness: ﴿Blessed﴾, meaning He is exalted, sanctified, and high [and magnified], and He is established in a stability without equal, with blessing, abundance and continual goodness and loftiness.

Since the one who possesses dominion may not be able to keep it in his hand, or give what he wants of it to another, or withdraw it from him whenever he wishes, He said: ﴿He in whose hand is the dominion﴾, meaning by His power and disposal, not by the power of another; ﴿the dominion﴾, meaning the matter that manifests the world; so to Him belongs every management of it and every management within it, and by His power is the manifestation of what He wills; there is no preventer for Him from anything, and no equal to Him in any respect. It is a metaphor for encompassing and dominance. Mention of the hand is only for depicting encompassing and complete power, since it is [its locus], together with transcendence above bodily members and above everything that conveys need or resemblance to creation.

Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr [the Imam] said: The occurrence of what this surah opens with, of transcendence and attributes of exaltedness, comes only after a detailing and presentation of the wonders of His making, glorified is He, like the occurrence of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿So blessed be God, the best of creators﴾, after the detailing of human transformation from the time of his creation from an extract of clay to His producing him as another creation. Likewise every such occurrence not found within any [surah] has been singled out for transcendence and informing of attributes of exaltedness [and] majesty.

Since at the end of Surah al-Tahrim He had placed what contains the greatest lesson for whoever remembers, and the highest sign for whoever gains insight, from the mention of two women who were under two of Our righteous servants whom God sent [as mercy to His servants] and who strove in calling people, and He forbade seeking light through their light or refuge in their guidance to anyone who was not among those closest to them or more witnessing of the signs and great miracles through which they were supported; and despite that they did not avail them anything against God; then this admonition was followed by what He placed at one edge of it and an opposite of its state, namely the mention of Pharaoh's wife, whom the sin of her companion and his great audacity did not deceive, despite the severity of the bond and the continuity of intimacy, because of what had preceded for her in eternal knowledge of happiness and great mercy; so she said: ﴿My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise﴾ [al-Tahrim: 11]. In these two stories there is the presentation of a cause of mercy whose grasp was forbidden to those most closest to it in apparent matters, and the presentation of a cause of trial from which the one closest to entanglement was protected; then He followed that with a story free of these two causes and separate in its beginnings from those two stories, namely the mention of Maryam daughter of Imran, so that the intelligent person may know where to place causes, and that hearts are in the hand of the Mighty, the Giver, Exalted is He, followed that.

With His true word: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion, and He is over all things Powerful﴾. If the King, glorified and exalted is He, has the dominion in His hand, then He is the One who gives dominion and grace to whomever He wills, removes it from whomever He wills, honors whomever He wills, and humbles whomever He wills, as the other verse in Al 'Imran expressly states. Thus the connection of Surah al-Mulk with what precedes it has become clear. Then Surah al-Mulk was built upon admonition and reflection, by spreading out the proofs and setting up the demonstrations, as the tafsir spreads out. End of quote.

Since the one who disposes of dominion may not have complete or general power, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He﴾, meaning He alone, has a greatness that dominates hearts and a governance that encompasses every acquisition of benefit and repelling of harm, because He is ﴿over all things﴾, meaning He enables whomever He wills to have dominion and other things, from its inner dimension, which is the malakut, and other than it, of what exists and what does not exist; ﴿Powerful﴾, meaning of perfect power. He indicated this by His saying:

[p. 220] **﴿Who created﴾**, i.e., decreed and brought into being.

Since fear of being inflicted with pain is more conducive to humility, and because it is a stronger indication of sovereignty, while the original state of things is non-existence, he placed ﴿death﴾ first, meaning this category, which is the cessation of life from a living being. This is the one who is most capable of transformation, by making him inanimate as though he had never had any movement at all. The first thing He does in that abode, after each group has settled in its own abode, is to annihilate this category, so it is slaughtered after being shaped in the form of a ram. ﴿And life﴾, i.e., this category, which is the meaning by which the inanimate is empowered to move by itself and by will. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Death, Allah created it in the form of a white-speckled ram that does not pass by anything or find its smell without dying. And life is in the form of a horse with a bridle, which Jibril and the prophets used to ride, so that nothing finds its smell without coming to life. It is the one from whose trace al-Samiri took a handful and cast it upon the ornaments that the Children of Israel had thrown, and he intended it to become a calf [so it became a calf].

Since he mentioned the indicator of power, he followed it with its purpose, which is judgment, the defining trait of kings. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿that He may test you﴾, i.e., He deals with you, and He knows you better than you know yourselves, in the manner of one who tests in order to make manifest what you have of action by choice, ﴿as to which of you is best in deed﴾, i.e., in terms of action, meaning that his deed is better than the deeds of others. The Qur'an's expression in ascribing goodness to a human indicates that whoever's deed is better, he himself is better, even if he is the most unsightly of people in appearance; and whoever's deed is worse is the opposite of that. Goodness is only known through the Shari'a (revealed law); what the Shari'a has made good is good, and what it has made ugly is ugly. This is beneficial for upholding obedience, because whoever reflects on his own state knows that he is distinct from the rest of the animals by intellect, from plants by his life, and from inanimate things by his growth, and that this is not from himself, as shown by his death. So this was not for him except by a choosing agent, to whom life belongs of His own essence. So he strives for His pleasure by following His messengers, if he is intelligent, [p. 221] thanking Him when He bestows blessings, being patient when He tests and takes revenge, serving Him by what He commands, and restraining himself from what He forbids. This verse thus includes the existence of what calls for happiness, the absence of what prevents it, and the existence of what calls for it is preparation and guidance. Preparation is His, glorified is He, assisting the servant by preparing him to accept happiness, like the blacksmith who softens iron with fire so that it may accept becoming a knife. Guidance is His taking him by the forelock to what He has prepared him for, like striking with the knife and sharpening it for cutting. The absence of what prevents it is the removal of obstacles to that, which is the repelling of disturbing and corrupting things, like the blunting of the knife. This occurs through the means and the means of the means, which is what is contained in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "O Allah, help me and do not help against me," and the rest of the hadith. So his mention of the completeness of power and might, together with the mention of ﴿the best in deed﴾, indicates His granting him success in what was mentioned. Whoever reflects upon the verse knows that He did not create him except so that his essence might be distinguished from the sincerity of others, or his sincerity from the essence of others. And [that] this world is a field of sowing, and the Hereafter is a harvest. Thus he becomes, from himself, one who sees clearly. His will is stirred toward what he was created for: at times by looking at the beauty of his Lord in goodness and benevolence, at other times by looking at His majesty in power and capability, and at other times by looking at himself with compassion for it from the disgrace of deprivation. So he strives for the pleasure of his Lord and the rectification of his soul, fearing the consequence of this trial.

[p. 222] Since trial from us is only not neglected by one who is ignorant of consequences and incapable of turning the evildoer away from his evil and making him a doer of good from the beginning of his upbringing, He said, negating this of His unassailable majesty, after having negated it by His subtle management and His great affair in [the creation of] death and life, and removing by the attribute of might what one of strong resolve might say: "I do not need great exertion in reaching Him, exalted is He; rather I reach Him at whatever time I wish, with the easiest striving." ﴿And He is﴾, i.e., while the state is that He alone is ﴿the Mighty﴾, [i.e.,] the one to whom access is extremely difficult, from ʿizaz, which is the rugged place, [and] who overcomes everything while nothing overcomes Him. So if He willed to make all of them good-doers, He could; and He would not be like this unless He were of complete power. This entails complete knowledge, oneness, and necessary existence, eternally and everlastingly.

Since the mighty among us destroys everyone who opposes him when he knows of their opposition, He said, explaining His granting respite to the disobedient and encouraging the evildoer to repent, after warning him against persisting in sin, because he may consider himself contemptible, saying: "Someone like me is not fit for service, given my decisive sins, and where is dust from the Lord of lords?" ﴿The Forgiving﴾, i.e., that He, despite that, acts in erasing sins, both their traces and their effects, in the manner of one who is exceedingly thorough in that, and He receives whoever comes to Him in the best manner, as [p. 223] He, exalted is He, said in the sacred hadith (hadith qudsi, a saying of the Prophet in which Allah speaks in the first person, not part of the Qur'an): "Whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running."

When al-Biqa'i had established for Him, glory be to Him, the attributes of might and forgiveness in the most eloquent form, He indicated this by His saying, indicating the perfection of His singularity, after the signs within the souls, with the signs of the horizons, as guidance toward noble character: ﴿Who created﴾, that is, originated [according to this measure] without any prior model, ﴿seven heavens﴾ being ﴿in layers﴾, plural of ṭabaq (layer). Each one of them, because of its intense conformity with the other, seems to seek conformity with it, such that every part of it conforms to a part of the other, and no part of it lies outside that. They could only be so if the earth is a sphere and the lowest heaven encompasses it as the shell of an egg encompasses the egg from all sides, and the second encompasses the lowest, and so on until the Throne encompasses all. The Kursi, which is the nearest of them to it, in relation to it is like a ring cast into a desert; so what is your opinion of what is beneath it? Each heaven is named in relation to the one above it in this way. The people of astronomy (ahl al-hay'ah) have established that they are so, and there is nothing in the Sharia that contradicts it; rather its apparent meanings agree with it, especially the comparison to a ring cast into a desert, as the explanation of this has passed in the commentary on Surah al-Sajdah. God, exalted is He, encompassed the earth with its benefits from all sides, and placed the center such that it draws the lower to itself; so however the animal walks on its sides, the center requires that its feet be toward the earth and its head toward the sky, so that the sky is always, in its view, above, and the earth is below, on whatever side it is upon. So glory be to the Subtle, the All-Aware. There is no doubt that whoever reflects on this greatness, together with the kindness He has shown us in what He has prepared in it for us of benefits, He has chosen him with love and set him apart from every opposite, so he cleaves to Him in supplication and relies on none but Him in every repelling and every bringing of benefit, and hastens toward what pleases Him and what He loves in every ease and hardship.

Since that in itself is beyond the capacity of the created, and since the thickness of each heaven is a five-hundred-year journey, and the distance between every two heavens is likewise, with no gaps, pillars, or tent-ropes, this was the utmost in departing from custom in itself. And because it has been said that a dome built without gaps, and without anything through which air enters, becomes corrupt and collapses, He indicated His might through the greatness of His making in that by describing it, saying: ﴿You see no discrepancy in﴾ and the original would have been "its creation," but He indicated His might and the generality of His greatness by saying: ﴿the creation of the Most Merciful﴾, that is, of it and of other than it. Had it not been for His mercy and the generality of His greatness, which required honoring His creation after forgiving them for the deficiencies they have, how beautifully He has been kind to them through it, in its vastness, its adornment, and the benefits in it. He intensified the negation by His saying: ﴿any imperfection﴾ between the small of that creation and its large, in relation to the Creator, in His bringing it into being in one equal manner. His saying "to it" is only: when He wills a thing, He says to it "Be," and it is. There is no difference in this between the atom, for example, and the mountain, nor in relation to the Creator between the incapacity of their small and large to originate anything from nonexistence, whether small or great, grand or lowly. You will not see any imperfection in the creation, such that some of it would be out of harmony with another through contradiction, turmoil, or conflict in its form, not suited to it, such that it is outside of it or repugnant to it in the requirement of wisdom, the traces of goodness in craftsmanship, falling short of perfection and coherence, departing from firm order and agreement, and indicating to the Creator the perfection of power and to the created the fact of having come into being, through some kind of weakness of structure, such that each one is like one seeking to oppose the other, or intending to make the other fail and oppose it. This is according to the reading that omits the alif and doubles the letter (tafāwut), such that difference among paired things and non-equality appears as if it were intended in itself and as a primary aim. Rather, opposition is found only rarely, such that one knows that harmony is what is intended in itself and as a primary aim; so if some opposition occurs in something of it, it is in a rare manner, so that one knows it is not intended in itself, but that it is meant to indicate choice, and that the agent is the capable chooser, not mere nature. Al-Razi said: "It is as if tafāwut is the thing that differs from the arrangement of the order." Al-Baghawi said: "from crookedness, disagreement, and contradiction." Another said: "lack of proportion, as if some of a thing escapes another and does not suit it, and it is from fawt, which is that some of it escapes some other because its equality is scarce." Abu Hayyan said: "Tafāwut is exceeding the limit which requires addition or subtraction." End.

This becomes clear in that most creatures are hollow, and the hollow thing is made flat, then folded, and one of its sides is joined to the other, so there is a kind of seam that people of skill recognize, even if its maker strives to conceal it; and if there are opposite things in it, there is some disparity in them, however little, even if the maker strives for equality. But God's creation has no disparity in any way. The heavens are spherical, and you see in no part of them a crack or a visible or hidden split. The animal is hollow, and you see in no part of its body a break in which the folding and hollowing occurred; each of its two opposites is equal to the other, like the two eyes, the two ears, the two nostrils, the two shins and the like, in which equality is intended, with no disparity at all. And there are other things whose explanation would be long and which cannot be fully enumerated. So glory be to Him whose power has no end, so His capabilities have no end, and whose knowledge cannot be counted in any way. All this is easy for Him, and the matter in this is clear and manifest. This is with the vastness whose measure cannot be grasped, namely that each heaven, in relation to the one above it, is like a ring cast into a desert, until one reaches the Kursi, then the Great Throne. Whoever is pleased that they are so, the benefit obtained from all that is in them of stars, moist or dry, or illuminated, and connections raining and fixed, all of which flows from them in a steady order and an unbroken system, its flow measured with justice, arranged for the benefits of existence and the interests of all beings, held upon a subtle air by a noble governance: none of them exceeds its station or passes its limit, nothing beneath it sinks from the air and falls, nor rises from its place by the weight of an atom and floats. He has encompassed all of them in command and governed them, humbled under His dominion.

Since the knowledge arising from beauty is the most noble of knowledge, He indicated the wonder of what He mentioned through sensory observation of it as such. He therefore linked to it His saying, alerting through repeated returning that everyone observes that in this way from the time he understands until he reaches the limit of responsibility, which requires being addressed by this speech: ﴿Then return the sight﴾, that is, after your repeating it before that. He indicated by directing the address toward the most perfect of creation, ﷺ, in hearing, sight, and insight, and every meaning, that there is no doubt in it.

Since asking about a thing indicates intense concern to investigate it, He alerted that this is something the earlier ones were intensely concerned with, and so He said: ﴿Do you see﴾, that is, in any of them.

Since this interrogative implies negation, He intensified the negation by His saying: ﴿any rifts﴾, that is, flaws, by cracks, splits, or otherwise, to contradict what they are upon and what they have reported of their harmony, cohesion, and straightness, which is their due, indicating the might of what is in them and the far-reaching forgiveness of Him. This also indicates that each of them encompasses what is beneath it, for if they had gaps, the benefits arranged for them would be lost, the stars scattered through their layers, or some of them, or all of them. The air and all benefits are confined within them, enclosed, moving and disposed within them according to the governance; and the animal in the air is like the fish in water. Were the air withdrawn from it, it would die, just as if the water were withdrawn from the fish, it would die.

Since the context concerns recompense for righteous and wicked deeds, and the absence of retribution against the wrongdoers in this world indicates that it will occur after resurrection, and since (His) might necessitates this, and since His creation of this existence in this order establishes it, and since their deeds were those of one who denies it, especially their declaration that there is no resurrection, He indicated the greatness of His might through what He originated of this lofty, wondrous canopy, then by making it preserved with this impregnable preservation over the succession of ages and the recurrence of years. So He said, using the particle of delay (thumma) to signify His majesty through the continuance of repetition over long time: ﴿Then return the gaze﴾. And He confirmed what the verse conveys of the demand for repetition by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿twice﴾, meaning two more times. This is its linguistic meaning. But considering the context, it is known that the return is time after time, continuing to repeat this in search of a flaw, without end, just as "labbayk" is meant as answering without end. This is indicated by His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿will return to you﴾, meaning without choice, but by overpowering, exhaustion and defeat, ﴿the gaze, dazed﴾, meaning humbled, expelled, [abased], far from attaining what is sought, ﴿while it is﴾, meaning while the state is that it is ﴿weary﴾, meaning dulled, exhausted from the length of repetition, the fine scrutiny of the gaze and the distance of the field of vision. If this is the state in some of what is made, how then would one seek knowledge of the Maker in His perfection from His majesty and beauty? How then of one who utters incarnation or union? Enough for him is Hell, and wretched is the resting place.

(p-230) When He, glorified is He, had informed of the wondrous nature of this creation, drawn attention to some of its subtleties, and commanded looking and repeated looking, and since the listener's gaze first turns toward the sky for its nobility, its strange making, its wondrous arrangement, and its lofty elevation, he was in a state of expecting information about this adornment with which it has been studded, He said, in answer to [what -] would arouse his expectation, emphasizing with an oath to inform that the intelligent person should keep far from denying anything of the perfection attributed to the Possessor of this creation, [connecting it -] to what its implication is: "Indeed, this extent suffices as proof of the greatness of the Originator of this making and the completeness of His power." ﴿And indeed﴾ He sought to draw gratitude by bringing pleasures, and said, looking at the station of greatness, diverting minds from what "the Most Merciful" (al-Rahman) requires of the generality of mercy, as a reminder of what is in the previous verse, and as an alert to what is in the adornment with the stars of their being mixed with the meteors, which is the punishment of "the rebellious, insolent jinn": ﴿We have adorned﴾, a further indication that points to greatness after that first indication, ﴿the nearest heaven﴾, that is, the nearest of the heavens to the earth, which is the one that witnesses, and you always see it, and it is the ceiling of the house in which you have gathered in this worldly life, ﴿with lamps﴾, that is, very great blazing stars, whose number exceeds counting, apparent, moving, luminous, shining. They are the planets that light the earth at night with the illumination of the lamp with which you adorn the ceilings of your houses, so they yield a portion of the light of morning. The adorning with them does not prevent them from being fixed in the heaven above [the heavens -], and they appear to us according to the transparency (of the celestial bodies' clarity) and the brightness of those lamps from their intense light.

When He, whose power is majestic, had informed of His great power in them, alerting to what in them brings pleasure through those lights and to guidance in religion and the world, which, were it not for them, no one would benefit fully in a night, He informed of what is in them along with the adornment of averting harms, in a general expression, even though the intended is the greater part, for what the meteors have is other than what serves guidance and markers. So He said: ﴿And We have made them﴾, that is, the stars, insofar as [they are -] by Our greatness, together with their being an adornment and signs for guidance, ﴿missiles﴾, plural of *rujm*, which is both a verbal noun and a noun for what is hurled with it. ﴿For the devils﴾, those who deserve expulsion, distance, and burning from the jinn, because of the burning they undergo. This is an explanation of Our greatness and a guarding of the nearest heaven, which is the place where Our command of decree and destiny descends, and the sending down of this wise Reminder, lest they corrupt the true religion of people by eavesdropping on it from there, and confuse their affair by mixing the truth with which We sealed the religions with falsehood, so they bring them out, since they are their enemies, from light into darkness, [as -] they were in the Age of Ignorance. And with what He, glorified is He, created in its temperaments of moistening and drying, heat and cold, and moderation from which the four seasons arise, and the subjugation by which there is rising and setting, motion and rest, by which is known what the outcome is, from what the messengers informed of regarding the passing away, along with what indicates the night and the day, the evening and the morning (p-232), and things whose description fails in their essences and in counting their benefits, to the extent that if anything in the heavens that the Wise has arranged for the welfare of this world were lost, every animal and plant on the face of the earth would perish. The meteor by which they are stoned is separated from the fire of the stars, and it remains in its orbit in a state like a brand of fire taken from them, while they remain in their state without diminishing. This justifies calling them *rujum*. So whoever a meteor reaches among them, it kills him or breaks his affair and deranges him. It may also be that what is meant is conjectures of the human devils, who are the astrologers, speaking by them as guessing about the unseen in matters that are among the great trials, so that the one with certainty may be distinguished from the wavering and the knower from the ignorant. In al-Bukhari, Qatada said: "The stars were created for three purposes: an adornment for the sky, missiles against the devils, and signs by which one is guided. Whoever interprets them otherwise has erred, lost his share, and burdened himself with what he has no knowledge of."

Since the sense is: and We pelted them with them in actuality when they eavesdropped, to distance them from the dwelling of the honored ones, the place of purity and intimacy, and the descent place of decree and destiny, and as a deterrent to others like them, a punishment for them in this world, He followed it with His saying, as a warning from His majesty after He had encouraged desire for His great beauty: ﴿And We have prepared﴾, that is, We have readied in the Hereafter, alongside this (p-233) which is in this world, by Our greatness, ﴿for them﴾, that is, the devils who steal hearing, ﴿the punishment of the blaze﴾, that is, the fire [-] which is at its utmost blazing. So in the verse is good news for the people of hearing, sight, and intellect, and in it is an alert that is not hidden.

When Allah, glory be to Him, informed us of His preparing the punishment for them specifically, He also informed us of His preparing [the fire] for every doer according to their deeds, in a manner that includes them within it. So He said, urging disbelief in His great retribution, which is outside the custom in that it is not extinguished, since it is not a sword, nor a staff, nor a whip or the like, but the fire, which is outside the custom in that it is not extinguished. The one being punished has no path or hope of escaping from it [but -], rather, whenever time lengthens, it meets him with intensity and continuation. How wretched is the gathering of blameworthy things in every retribution, together with humiliation and contempt. ﴿And for those who disbelieve﴾ [i.e., who brought about -] the concealment of what [of -] its right is to appear and be made manifest, namely submission to God. So He said, turning the speech away from the station of majesty to the attribute of beneficence specific to nurture, as an alert to the great ingratitude contained in their denial: ﴿in their Lord﴾, i.e., the One who alone originated them and showed kindness to them, so they denied His bringing them into being after death, and that is disbelief on their part in what they witnessed of His bringing them forth from non-existence. ﴿the punishment of Hell﴾, i.e., the fiery abode that will meet them with scowling, frowning and wrath.

Since the implied sense was "it is their destination," He said, indicating that they will never be released from it at all, ever and forever: ﴿and wretched is the destination﴾, i.e., it.

When he had described their condemnation with a comprehensive term of blame, he followed it with a description of one aspect of their scowling (tajahhum) as a giving of reason (ta'lil). He said, indicating through the verb of casting the baseness and worthlessness of these people, and using the particle of certainty (ada al-tahqiq) to show that it is a matter that must occur, and with the passive form to show that casting them into it is extremely easy for anyone who is commanded to do it: ﴿When they are cast therein﴾, meaning the disbelievers [and] the base ones are thrown, by whatever thrower We command to cast them, ﴿therein﴾, when the angels drag them and throw them as firewood is thrown into the fire, ﴿they will hear from it﴾, meaning from Hell itself, ﴿a roar﴾, meaning a terrifying sound more hideous than the first sound of a donkey, because of its intense blazing and seething. Or it refers to its people, with an omitted modifier (mudaf) understood. ﴿And it boils up﴾, meaning it seethes with them as a cauldron seethes with what is in it [from] the intensity of flaming and blazing. So they continue in it, ascending and descending, like a bucket when [the water] is boiling in it, with no resting place for them at all.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 67, verse 8:

When He described it as roaring (fawarān), He explained its cause, as a figure for the intensity of its blazing against them, saying: ﴿It almost bursts with rage﴾. That is, it comes close to (taqaruba) [from -] that some of it separates from (p-235) some other part, as one says: "So-and-so almost bursts with anger," and "So-and-so became angry, so a piece of him flew to the earth and a piece to the sky," as a metaphor (kināyah) for the intensity of anger. ﴿From rage﴾, that is, against them. It is as if one of the two tā's (of the verb) was dropped, indicating that there occurs [from it -] a separating and joining in a manner of such speed that it can hardly be perceived as it truly should be. All of this is due to the anger of its master. It will come on the Day of Resurrection, led to the gathering place with a thousand bridles, each bridle held by seventy thousand angels who drive it with it. It is of such intensity of rage that it overpowers the angels and charges at the people, cutting through all the bridles and crushing the people of the gathering place. Nothing turns it back from them except the Prophet ﷺ, who confronts it with his light, and it turns back. Yet each angel has such strength that if he were commanded to uproot the earth and what is on it of mountains and lift it up into the air, he would do so without any difficulty. This is like how it was extinguished in this world with a single breath, as narrated by the group (al-Jama'ah) except al-Tirmidhi. This is the wording of Abu Dawud, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: "The sun eclipsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ - and he mentioned his prayer until he said: then he blew in the last of his prostration. He said: 'Uff, uff! Did You not promise me that You would not punish them while I am among them, and they are seeking forgiveness?'" And in the narration of al-Nasa'i, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The Fire was brought so near to me that I began to push it back, fearing that it would overtake you."

When He mentioned their state, He followed it with their state in the torment of the heart through their belief (p-236) that they were wrongdoers in some respect. He explained the cause of their punishment as a deterrent from it, so He said: ﴿Whenever﴾. Since the verb (al-munki') means mere casting, it was made passive (bunya li-l-maf'ūl) to indicate that, and to indicate their insignificance by the ease of their being cast, His words: ﴿a group is cast into it﴾, that is, into Jahannam, by the Zabaniyah pushing them, those who are more enraged against them than the Fire itself. ﴿A group﴾, that is, a company who are in the utmost haste, rushing, their insides trembling from the intensity of the driving. ﴿Its keepers asked them﴾, that is, that group asked the keepers ﴿of it﴾, that is, of the Fire, a question of rebuke, reproach and terror.

Since it was as if it were said: "What was their question?", He said: They said, rebuking them, reproaching them, arguing against them regarding their deserving of punishment, adding to their torment by tormenting their spirits after tormenting their bodies: ﴿Did there not come to you﴾, that is, in the world, ﴿a warner﴾, that is, one who warns you, this Qur'an, and reminds you of what befell you and what befell those before you of the destroyed nations, because of your denial of the signs, and who recites to you the sent-down Books.

﴿They said, "Yes."﴾ Since this answer matched the question, the listener anticipated its clarification. They made it explicit, spelling out what it implied, in lamentation over themselves for what had befallen them and in regret. So they said: ﴿Indeed a warner has come to us﴾. They stated the position of the pronoun explicitly, for emphasis and specification, and said: ﴿a warner﴾, meaning one who warns with intense admonition. ﴿So we denied﴾, meaning that as a consequence of his coming, we inflicted denial upon everything the warner said (p. 237). ﴿And we said﴾, meaning, adding to the denial, to the provocation against him, and to the obstinacy whose ill omen fell upon us: ﴿"God has not sent down anything"﴾, meaning, the One who possesses all perfection, upon you [ not -] upon anyone else. Perhaps the use of the intensive form (al-tafʻil, the doubled-consonant verb form) indicates their denial of the act as a matter of choice, which entails gradualness (al-tadrij, progression by stages). Exalted is God far above that, with great exaltedness. They went to extremes in the negation, so they said: ﴿"anything"﴾, neither revelation nor anything else. This wickedness did not suffice them, so they said, emphasizing: ﴿"You are only"﴾, meaning, "not" [ ... ] [in the sense of "in" (in) being "ma"].

Since their denial of one messenger amounted to denial of all the messengers, they said, out of obstinacy: ﴿"You"﴾, meaning, O warners mentioned in "a warner", where the word is meant generically. The address in the plural also indicates that the response of all of them to all was uniform, despite their separation in time, to the point that it was as though they had [ upon -] an appointment. ﴿"Only in manifest error"﴾, meaning, a distance from the path, error, and a blindness encompassing you ﴿"great"﴾. So we exaggerated in denial and folly through mockery and contempt.

When He, glory be to Him, related what they said to the keepers of Hell out of regret for themselves, He related what they said afterwards among themselves, adding to their grief and to their own loathing of themselves. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they will say﴾, that is, the disbelievers, in rebuking themselves: ﴿Had we been listening or using our intellect﴾, that is, with what is innate to us (al-gharīza, natural disposition).

Since hearing is the greatest of the faculties of the intellect (ʿaql), on which religious accountability (taklīf) depends, they said: ﴿Had we been listening﴾, that is, a hearing that benefits by accepting the truth and rejecting falsehood, ﴿or using our intellect﴾, that is, with what the sense of hearing and other senses conveyed to us, an intellect that would have saved us, even if there had been no hearing (p-238). They limited the two verbs to show that what they had of hearing and intellect amounted to nothing, since it did not avert this affliction for them by accepting from the messengers what they reminded them of, the counsel of their Lord and the testimony of the clear signs. ﴿We would not have been﴾, that is, continuously, ﴿among the companions of the blaze﴾, that is, among those for whom the Fire has been prepared, which is at the utmost of kindling, heat, flaming and blazing, to the point that it seems to be in a frenzy. He decreed their eternal abiding in its company. The greatest part of this torment is that they were forced to undertake the rebuke of themselves and their loathing of themselves, since it will not be accepted from them. This departs from the custom in this world, where when a person shows humility by acknowledging his fault, blaming himself and being fair, he is shown mercy and his repentance is accepted.

In this verse is the greatest virtue of the intellect. Ibn al-Muhabbar related in the Book of the Intellect, and al-Ḥārith (related) from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "For everything there is a support, and the support of the believer is his intellect. In proportion to his intellect is his worship. Have you not heard the saying of the wicked: ﴿Had we been listening or using our intellect, we would not have been among the companions of the blaze﴾."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 67, verse 11:

Since this confession would only increase their harm, whereas it would have benefited them had they said it in the abode of action (dar al-'amal) and regretted it and given it up, he (God) made the following statement a consequence of it, adding to what preceded of the torment of their spirits through the angels' detestation of them, and then their detestation of themselves, the detestation of God toward them: ﴿So they will admit﴾, meaning they went to the extreme, combining with the detestation of God and His angels toward them their detestation of themselves, in the admission, which is confession from knowledge.

Since the one who brought them to ruin was disbelief, from which all sins branch out, He mentioned it singly, saying, exalted is He: ﴿for their sin﴾, meaning in the abode of recompense (dar al-jaza'), just as they used to go to extremes in denial in the abode of action, so it did not benefit them because its place had passed. Or, He did not gather the sin as a sign that they were all at one level in going to extremes in denial, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Thus did there not come to those before them any messenger but they said, "A magician or a madman."﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 52] ﴿Did they bequeath this to one another? Rather, they are a transgressing people.﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 53] Or the singular form is more intense in warning against many sins and few, the trivial and the grave.

Since they had gone to extremes in both abodes in distancing themselves from the places of mercy and lowering themselves to the state of wrath, this produced and caused his statement: ﴿So away﴾, meaning distance in the direction of the lowest part, and it is a curse upon them that is answered, ﴿for the companions of﴾, and more evident as a warning of its great blaze, its fury and its threat, so He said: ﴿the Blaze﴾, meaning the one whose fuel their deeds have decreed they must remain in.
