Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 67, verse 12:

When Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned the people of ascription to might (al-'izza) because of the might that they attained, He followed them with their opposites, those who subdue their souls (al-mutawwi'in anfusahum) to the indication of the intellect ('aql), who are qualified for the description of knowledge (ma'rifa). He said, emphasizing it because of the denial that the opposites deserve: ﴿Indeed, those who fear﴾, that is, who dread [with a fear that makes their hearts tender and makes others tender, such that they are like a lover of one who is hated, who finds no settled rest because of their expectation of punishment. Whenever they increase in obedience, they increase in dread]. They give what they give while their hearts are fearful, so they guard themselves against the blazing of the Fire upon them. He turned away from the context of majesty, which is all-encompassing, to the attribute of beneficence, to draw attention to the fact that the looking at beneficence overcame them, and it led them to gratitude, together with what the dread indicated of their being characterized by the distinction that brought them to terror. So He said: ﴿their Lord﴾, who was good to them by developing them, through what He placed for them of means, in the stages of goodness. If they dread Him while looking at the attribute of His beneficence, then what do you think of them when they look at the attributes of His retribution? ﴿unseen﴾, that is, while they are absent from Him, glory be to Him, and His threat is absent from them, while they are absent from the eyes of people. Fear has filled what is absent from them of people, which is their hearts. So they speak with people while their hearts are burning with the fires of fear and are struck by the swords of awe. Thus they abandon disobedience where no one among people sees them! This is not possible for them except through great discipline, because of the powers in people that call for rebellion.

Some of the knowers said: In the human being there are qualities that demand knowledge of what mixes with them of appetites, and from them there arises, and Allah forbid, the contention over greatness, majesty, sublimity and beauty. The heart demands sole existence, command and prohibition. There is no one who does not inwardly hold what Pharaoh said, but he does not find room for it as Pharaoh found it. The intellect, in its management and its influence, demands the belief that if it were given existence it would manage it, and it sees that its management is the management, even if the most corrupt corruption results. Thus it continues to say: "If it were so, it would be so." The self does not imagine that it has such strength and power that if it wished to ruin cities and build them, it would do so. So let the human being beware, for his most hostile enemy is his own self, which is between his two sides. Whenever he leaves it, it spreads. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿Nay, indeed man transgresses﴾ [al-'Alaq: 6] ﴿when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-'Alaq: 7], and forgets what comes after it: ﴿Indeed, to your Lord is the return﴾ [al-'Alaq: 8]. For this reason some of the Persian kings, who were the most intelligent of kings, would appoint a man who would be behind him, close to him, [who would say to him] whenever his armies gathered after every little while: "You are a slave," and he would keep repeating that, and the king would say to him each time he said it: "Yes." So it is incumbent upon the intelligent person to subdue his self so that it returns at peace, by being pleased with Allah as Lord, in order to enter into the bondage of servitude, and with Islam as religion, in order to become firmly rooted in it. Then greatness does not contend with the king over his cloak, nor majesty over his garment, nor sublimity over his crown, nor beauty over his robe. He does not contend with Him over what He manages of laws, what He makes manifest of knowledge, and what He judges over His servants by His decree and His destiny.

Since dread points to sins, and what matters most to them is relief from them, Allah, exalted, said: ﴿For them is forgiveness﴾, that is, a great covering that encompasses all their sins.

Since joy is only complete through giving, He said: ﴿and a reward﴾, that is, from the bounty of Allah, ﴿great﴾, which will be for them of honor such that it makes them forget the severe pains they endured in the world, and beside it the worldly pleasures become small.

Then He indicated this by His saying, marvelling at those who hesitate even slightly over it, and rebuking them for affirming knowledge and negating its opposite in the most emphatic manner: ﴿Does He not know﴾, that is, everything that can be known. The object is omitted for generality. Then He mentioned the Agent, describing Him by what brings the one informed of Him closer to comprehension, saying: ﴿He who created﴾, that is, the One who brought into existence creation, from the hearts that contain secrets and the bodies and other things, and impressed upon each of these whatever was impressed, of what He had decreed by His knowledge and perfected by His wisdom, for every maker knows best what he has made. It is also permissible, and it is the better view, that ﴿who﴾ (man) be the object and the agent be implicit, meaning: Does not God know His creation absolutely, and He possesses the attributes of subtlety (al-lutf) and awareness (al-khabar), whose nature is to perceive inner things in a way that is not like anything else? This is because the purpose is to affirm knowledge of what they concealed, since they supposed that if they kept it secret it would remain hidden, not to affirm knowledge in an absolute sense, for they did not deny that. ﴿And He is﴾, that is, while the case is that He is ﴿the Subtle﴾ [that is], the One who knows what He has set within the hearts, for He reaches things through their opposites, so how could other matters escape Him? ﴿the Aware﴾, that is, of perfect knowledge of outward and inward things, so how could anything escape Him? This is the greatest of warnings, for whoever knows that the one he disobeys is aware of him and able over him will never disobey Him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 67, verse 15:

Since that is an obscure matter, He indicated it by a visible matter, which He originated by His subtle kindness and perfected by His expertise, in order to elicit gratitude from His servants for what He originated for them and bestowed upon them of the manifest blessings by which their subsistence is maintained. Were it not for Him, they would have no survival. So He said, resuming: ﴿He it is who made for you﴾, that is, He alone, ﴿the earth﴾ so that you may reach what benefits you, ﴿subservient﴾ (dhalul), that is, made subjugated and not resisting, submissive to being led by you to what you desire from it, of walking, extracting water, planting grain, planting trees, and other things, in the utmost submission, as the intensive form implies, even though in it there are soft places in which feet sink and whatever mixes with it sinks, and places intertwined with trees, where passage is impossible or difficult, and places full of beasts of prey, serpents, and other obstacles, and places that are towering mountains, either passage through them is impossible, like the mountain of the Barrier between us and Gog and Magog, concerning which it is reported in a hadith that feet slip upon it and do not stand firm, or passage through them is made arduous; and places that are seas, sweet or salty. Had He willed, He would have made all of it thus, so that it would be in a state where no benefit could be derived from it. Yet He did not divide it into plains, mountains, deserts, seas, rivers, springs, salt and sweet, crops and trees, soil and stone, sand and clay, and other things, except for a profound wisdom and a manifest power, so that it would be receptive to all that you desire from it, suitable for everything that benefits you in it.

Since the meaning of subjugation is what preceded, He ground upon it His saying, as an illustration of the purpose of subjugation, because the shoulders of a camel and the junction of them from the withers are the most delicate thing and the least suited to be trodden upon by the rider's foot and leaned upon: ﴿So walk﴾ [that is,] at ease, whether earning or not earning, if you wish, without a hardship that would make you leap or crawl, ﴿in its shoulders﴾, that is, its places which, were it not for Our facilitating the shoulders of the animals for you, they would shrink from standing upon, let alone walking. [And] Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: they are the mountains, because their subjugation is the strongest proof of the subjugation of other than them. Let your walking and your dealings in them be with humility, tranquility and calm, belittling yourselves and thankful to the One who subjected these to you. And Allah is the Guide.

When He mentioned, glory be to Him, that He made it easy for them to walk, He reminded them that He made it easy for them to bring forth good things and blessings, so He said: ﴿And eat﴾, and by His saying ﴿of His provision﴾ He indicated that the provision is beyond sufficiency, that is, the provision which He deposited for you in it and enabled you to extract, in contrast to what you know of your own conditions, for burying in the earth spoils what is buried and transforms it into its substance, as happens to one whom you have entombed in it. Despite that, you bury grain and other things that benefit you, and He, glory be to Him, brings them out for you in the best form you desire, and there come out for you foods, fruits, oils and garments that you know. Likewise the souls are difficult like mountains, and if you lead them to good they will be led by you, as it has been said: "The soul is what you accustom it to; it becomes accustomed."

Since the implied sense is an exhortation to gratitude and a warning against disbelief: and worship Him as recompense for His kindness to you and His nurturing of you, from Him is the origin of all of that, He followed it with what calls to shame before the Master and to embarrassment from His rebuke at the time of meeting Him, so He said: ﴿And to Him﴾, that is, Him alone, ﴿is the resurrection﴾, which is the bringing forth of all the living beings that the earth consumed and decayed, bringing them out at the time He wills, in the state each of them was in at death, just as He brought out those provisions; there is no difference between this and that. Except that you do not reflect, [so that He would] question you about what you used to do. So how fortunate is he who gives thanks, and how ruinous for him who disbelieves! For this is the most effective thing to prompt gratitude and the most powerful thing to keep one far from disobedience, especially disbelief, given what He has established of man's need and His kindness to him through all kinds of kindness.

When, after the appeal (to mercy), nothing remained but warning against opposition, He said, threatening those who deny with a punishment other than the punishment of Hell, and rebuking them for feeling secure after the proof had been established that sovereignty is in His hand, and that He is capable of what He wills from them, both through the means of His armies and without means. Having established man's need and weakness, He affirmed that he has [no fortress and no -] protector against God's punishment in any way, so he is constantly in need and bound to abasement: ﴿Do you feel secure﴾, i.e., O deniers. He addressed them in terms of what they believed, even though, [if -] one takes "rank" as the sense of "height" and interprets "heaven" as "elevation", or makes it a *kinayah* (metonymy, an indirect expression) for control, since custom generally holds that whoever is in something exercises control over it, the wording is valid without *ta'wil* (figurative interpretation). So He said: ﴿He who is in heaven﴾, i.e., according to your assumption that the Exalted, whose dominion overpowers you, is there. Or the meaning is: among the angels, the stern and severe ones whom He has deployed in the affairs of His servants. Or the meaning is: at the utmost height in rank. Or this indicates that in heaven is His greatest affair, since the deeds of His servants are raised up to it, it is the place of descent of revelation and the source of rain, the locus of holiness, sovereignty and majesty, the direction of the Throne, and the source of the purified and near angels whom God appointed to carry out His commands and prohibitions. What prompted such an acceptable interpretation, one current in the speech of the Arabs, is [the presence of -] the decisive proof that He, glory be to Him, is not confined to a direction, because He encompasses all things and cannot be encompassed, for that would only befit one in need. Then he replaced "min" (who) with an inclusive apposition (*badal ishtimal*), saying: ﴿that﴾.

Since His power to do what He wills without intermediary is like His power with intermediary, and His power when the intermediary is plural is like His power when it is singular, because the true doer in every case is He and no other, and [limited] by what the word "min" requires to indicate this meaning, whether by "min" is meant Him, glory be to Him, or His angels, or one of them, [so he said-]: ﴿will cause to sink﴾, i.e., do you feel secure from His causing it to sink? It is also permissible that by "min" is meant God, glory be to Him and exalted, as has passed, addressing them according to their assumption and suspicion that He is in heaven, and as a binding argument against them: just as He is capable of sending rain, causing growth, and other actions upon the earth, He is capable of other things. ﴿With you the earth﴾, as He caused Qarun and others to sink.

Since what is made to sink into the earth becomes like one falling through the air, [and what falls through the air -] begins to convulse, He mentioned this as a consequence in His saying: ﴿then behold, it﴾, i.e., the earth on which you are, ﴿quakes﴾, i.e., strikes, while it sinks with you and goes down into the air, swaying and tilting wherever God, glory be to Him, wills. (p-249) In *al-Qamus* (the lexicon): *al-mawr* is agitation, flowing over the surface of the earth, and movement.

When they might consider the sinking into the earth (al-khasfah) unlikely, and they were accustomed to what descends from the sky: dew, rain and thunderbolts, His saying ﴿Or do you feel secure﴾ is set in balance with that. That is, O you who deny. He repeated the mention of what they fear, for greater warning, saying: ﴿He who is in the heaven﴾ according to both interpretations ﴿that He may send against you﴾, that is, from the sky, ﴿a violent wind-storm (ḥāṣib)﴾, that is, [stones -] pelting you - that is, striking you - with them, along with a wind that is violent in its force, as happened to the people of Lot and the Companions of the Elephant (Aṣḥāb al-Fīl).

When this discourse was a great warning and an intense, eloquent admonition, and their condition before Him was wavering between turning toward and turning away, He made the following a consequence of it, on the assumption of their turning away through their persistence, with what is in man of deficiency. He said, threatening them with what cuts hearts, and turning the speech to the position of the first person to indicate the intensification of anger: ﴿So you will know﴾, that is, soon, with a promise that admits no failure, in this world and then in the Hereafter.

When knowledge of the modality of a thing is greater than knowledge of the mere existence of that thing, because knowledge of the former necessarily entails knowledge of the latter, and what one asks about in this way can only be something great, He said: ﴿how was My warning﴾, that is, My eloquent warning, when you witness the punishment, which is of such a kind that it cannot be withstood, and hopes do not attach to its removal or repelling. The letter yā' has been omitted from ﻧَذِيرِ (nadhīr) [and wāw -] from ﻧَكِيرٍ (nakīr), as an indication that, although it is outside the ordinary means, it is not the limit of His capacity; rather, with Him there is more, having no end in any respect and no bound.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 67, verse 18:

Since it is known that the one commanded to convey and warn them of this warning, ﷺ, is in the utmost mercy toward them [and compassion for them -], so that it grieves him in the extreme that the words of this speech imply their destruction if they do not believe, [and -] he loves to be patient with them, God, exalted is He, turned the address toward him, conjoining it to what is implied as its meaning: "So Our respite for them has been long, Our forbearance toward them has lasted, Our making them know of the greatness of Our power has continued, and they do not return. Our admonition to them has been abundant, and Our varying of speech among them through the tongues of Our messengers, upon them be blessings and peace, has been great, yet they persist in their transgression and do not desist." He said, depicting [for them -] what He threatened them with in a tangible matter, because visible things are more striking to a person, owing to his being bound by imagination, emphasizing the indication that denial, despite the establishment of proofs, is a matter that must be rejected, so that one hardly believes it: ﴿And certainly those before them denied,﴾ and transgressed, and oppressed, and turned away, and acted arrogantly, and rebelled, and turned their face [and heart] away ﴿those who﴾

Since this denial did not encompass all of the past peoples, He specified, saying: ﴿before them﴾, meaning the disbelievers of the past nations.

Since God, exalted is He, had given them respite and then seized them after a long forbearance, a seizing whose reports remained and whose traces had not been effaced until now despite the passing of time, it was such that one would ask about it because of the greatness of its circumstances, the severity of its earthquakes and the horror of its terrors. On account of this He said, drawing attention to calling that punishment to mind, even if only through asking about it: ﴿So how was My rejection?﴾, that is, My rejection of them, by what I afflicted them with of punishment, in its firmly established nature and the awfulness of its matter. Thus He combined consolation with the utmost threat.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 67, verse 19:

When He mentioned the fate of the earlier peoples, and the reminder of the hurling stones was a reminder to the Quraysh of what He had pelted their enemy, the Companions of the Elephant (Ashab al-Fil), with, in the recent past, by sending down upon them the birds in flocks (ṭayran ababil), it served as a warning to them not to persist in their disbelief and refuse to give thanks to Him. The implication was an affirmation of His power, the excellence of His management, and the subtlety of His nurture. He strengthened the birds, which are weak in themselves, enabling them to fly, so that by the generality of His mercy He might complete the means of their sustenance. This affirms that dominion is in His hand, and it is a warning against anyone disputing His management, while the speech is kept turned away from addressing them directly, to signal the severity of their reckoning and the evil of their final return and destination. "Have they not seen" refers to His power over the fates of the earlier peoples, the destruction of the deniers and the deliverance of the believers. He then connected to it his saying, turning away from them in order to increase the warning through the stoning by the birds and others: ﴿Have they not seen the birds above them﴾. The reciters agreed on reading it here with the third person (bi-l-ghayb), because the context is a response to the deniers, unlike the case in surah al-Nahl.

He indicated the far extent of the goal by the particle of ending, saying ﴿to the birds﴾, which is the plural of ṭā'ir.

Since the whole air is open for flight, He dropped the preposition and said ﴿above them﴾. He described the state of the birds in height by saying, describing them in the feminine to indicate their weakness in themselves were it not for His strengthening of them: ﴿spreading their wings﴾, meaning extending their wings, stretching them to the utmost extent so that they become level, without any bending. Moreover, when a group of them is together, they form ranks (ṣufūf), or a single rank in the utmost order, following a leader among them.

Since He expressed the rank by a noun, because it is the fixed origin, He expressed the movement by a verb, because flight in the expanse of the air is like swimming in the expanse of water. The basis of swimming is extending and spreading the limbs, and the folding is something that occurs after the spreading. So He said ﴿and folding them﴾, meaning they bring about the folding and spreading of the wings, time after time, for rest and for support in swimming through the air. When this estimation was complete in this manner, which is striking to hearts, He rendered it in the saying: ﴿What holds them up﴾, meaning in the air, in the state of folding and spreading, from falling, contrary to what their nature would require.

Since this is from the firm management that looks to the generality of mercy, He said: ﴿except the Most Merciful﴾, meaning the King whose mercy is general for everything, by preparing them, after He had bestowed upon them the mercy of bringing into existence, in various forms and distinct characteristics suited to moving through the air, with the forward and rear feathers and what else He created for them of the forms corresponding to that. The whole world is likewise: if He withheld His preservation of it for a single blink of an eye, it would be corrupted, with the spheres collapsing and the mountains crumbling and the rest. He expressed it in the surah al-Nahl with the Greatest Name, because its context is a refutation of the people of natures, namely the philosophers, who can be refuted only by one deeply versed in knowledge of all the principles of religion, through knowledge of all the meanings of the Most Beautiful Names and the Exalted Attributes, which are gathered in the name of the Essence.

Since this is a matter striking to the intellect, yet through intense familiarity it has become such that no one becomes aware of it except through being alerted, and since the ignorant person may suppose that the arrangement for flight is specific to birds, He, glory be to Him, drew attention to the greatness of what He prepared for the birds and that He is able to make this for others, by saying, emphasizing it because some minds fall short of believing it, and implying an association that is a challenge to the completeness of power, which in turn implies a challenge to the completeness of knowledge: ﴿Indeed He﴾, meaning the Most Merciful, glory be to Him, ﴿with everything﴾, whether small or great, whether majestic or insignificant, apparent or hidden, ﴿is All-Seeing﴾, reaching the utmost in sight and knowledge of the outward aspects of things and their inward aspects. Whatever He wills comes to be, and He creates wonders and brings into existence marvels, so He prepares whomever He wills among the children of Adam and others for such things.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 67, verse 20:

Since the implied sense, as an affirmation of that, is: "Who will manage your affairs, outwardly and inwardly, and who will inflict these kinds of punishment on those who denied before you?", he followed it with his words, returning to direct address because it is more effective in rebuke and reproach, and more indicative that the one addressed is not fit to be feared. He affirms [this] by saying ﴿Ammān﴾ ("Or who"), because He alone possesses dominion. He drew attention to the fact that the one who manages things must be extremely near to them and witnessing them, so that he is aware of their care, and that, along with his great nearness, he must be of high rank, such that he can be pointed to. So he said, affirming the helplessness of the servants: ﴿Hādhā﴾ ("This"), with the demonstrative of the present, ﴿alladhī﴾ ("who"). He brought out the returning pronoun explicitly, because it is necessary to make it explicit alongside the noun, since the noun is not suitable to bear the pronoun. So he said: ﴿huwa jundun﴾ ("is an army"), that is, a host and a helper. He turned the speech from the third person to the second person, because that is more emphatic in reproach, so he said: ﴿lakum yanṣurukum﴾ ("for you, to help you"), that is, against those who intend to harm you with being swallowed up by the earth, pelted with stones, and other such things. It is also possible that the implied sense is: "Is there for you a god who manages your affairs other than Us? Or is it the one who punished those who denied the messengers other than Us? Or is there for you an army to which one resorts, which will help you apart from Us?" As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Or do they have gods that protect them from Us?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 43]. But He presented it in the form of a question about specifying the army, to make known that, in their extreme ignorance, they believed that among the armies of the earth or the heavens there was someone who would help them; otherwise they would not have been secure.

(p-255) Since the ranks are all humble before His presence and extremely numerous, the Exalted said, pointing to that by the ḥarf (particle) and the ẓarf (adverbial expression of place), drawing attention to His, glorified is He, being above everything: no one has been able, or is able, to dispute with Him in that, nor in the fact that He encompasses everything below Him of the ranks: ﴿min dūn al-Raḥmān﴾ ("apart from the Most Merciful"), if He sends His punishment upon you. He stated the name explicitly and did not use a pronoun, to prompt the recollection of the all-encompassing mercy He possesses, and as an allusion to the threat that if He were to withhold it from anyone of those He brought into existence, the whole of His wrath would blind him. For this reason, He said, concluding from that, as an alert that the removal of harms and the gathering of benefits is only by His hand, because He alone possesses [dominion]: ﴿in﴾ ("not") — that is, mā — and He brought out the pronoun to generalize and to tie the judgment to the attribute, and to address them directly with that, because it is more fitting for rebuke. So He said: ﴿al-kāfirūn﴾ ("the disbelievers"), that is, those who are deeply immersed in disbelief, namely those who die upon it, ﴿illā fī ghurūr﴾ ("except in delusion"), that is, it has encompassed them, so there is no escape for them from it, and it is that they rely upon what is not a sound reliance.

(p-256) When He had presented the greatest of mercies, namely protection and support, which necessitate continued existence, He followed it with what completes that existence, saying: ﴿Or who﴾. He indicated nearness by the knowledge and distance by the exaltedness and greatness in His saying: ﴿this﴾. He indicated that everyone recognizes Him through His sublime attributes, from which His firm and sound actions arise, saying: ﴿[is it] He who﴾ [and He omitted the returning pronoun because the verb bears it for Him, saying: ﴿provides for you﴾]. That is, in a manner of continual renewal and persistence, His kindness never ceases, although He encompasses everything and is never heedless of anything. ﴿If He withholds His provision﴾ by withholding the causes from which it arises and through which it reaches you, as with rain. Even if provision were present, abundant, and easy to take, if God withheld from a person the strength to swallow, the people of the heavens and the earth would be unable to make that morsel palatable to him when he placed it in his mouth.

(p-257) When the proofs of His power and the comprehensiveness of His knowledge had been established, both in general and in particular, this was apt to make the denier turn back, the obstinate feel shame, the ignorant come to know, and the heedless awaken. Thus the situation called for the question: "Have they returned from their denial?" He followed this with His saying, turning the discourse to the third person as a way of turning away from them, to indicate the lowness of their rank, the badness of their understanding, and the strength of their heedlessness: ﴿Rather, they persist﴾, that is, they continued in folly, not in caution or courage. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': "Al-lajaj (persistence) is plunging into a matter despite many obstacles against it." ﴿in arrogance﴾, that is, immersed in obstinacy and pride against the truth, and in going out to gross corruption, ﴿and aversion﴾, that is, fleeing from good consideration and listening, which the natures call for. This took hold of them until it encompassed them, although none of them has any power to bring about benefit or to repel harm. What drives them to this is desire and anger.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 67, verse 22:

Since this is the act of one who has neither sight nor insight, he follows it with a statement that illustrates the monotheist and the polytheist as two travellers on two paths, each with his own religion: ﴿Is one who walks﴾, that is, continuously, ﴿prone (mukibban)﴾, that is, having thrown himself down and entered into falling, which is toppling, ﴿on his face﴾. This is a metaphor for walking on an unknown track and a crooked [crooked -] and faulty trail, contrary to the custom of rational people, because of a defect in his limbs and a disorder in his intellect and judgment. He stumbles every time and falls on his face, because for lack of reflection he walks through the most difficult places, since his desire inclines him away from the method that should be followed and ignorance dominates him. He is such that the repeated hardships do not deter him [for him -] from the cause that brings him into them. Glorified and exalted is He, who did not call his walking a "path," because he does not deserve that.

Since it may happen that one hits upon the easy way not through insight but by chance, He says: ﴿more guided (ahdá)﴾, that is, more rightly guided, ﴿Or one who walks﴾ constantly and steadily ﴿upright (sawiyyan)﴾, standing, holding his head high, facing forward, safe from stumbling, for by standing erect he sees what is in front of him, to his right and to his left, ﴿on a path (ṣirāṭ)﴾, that is, a well-trodden, wide, traversed, easy, straight road, ﴿straight (mustaqīm)﴾, that is, of the utmost straightness. This is the likeness of one who is content with God as Lord and with Islam as religion, for he follows the original sound nature (al-fiṭrah al-ūlā) free of desire, anger, or any trace of self-interest. The first is like the disbeliever, whose state in his journey to God is the state of one who prone (mukibb), that is, one who has thrown himself down on his face through extreme desire; he sees nothing around him, is not aware of what surrounds him, does not look at the signs, and takes no lesson from what is heard. So he is, in this world, something hidden, which will be exposed on the Day of Resurrection, and he will be gathered on his face into the Fire as a recompense for his contentment with this state in this abode. God, glorified is He, will then reveal to him what he concealed [for him -] today. The believer is the opposite in both respects.

This verse is an instance of ihtibāk (a rhetorical device in which each of two opposites is mentioned in one part and omitted in the other, being understood from its counterpart): He mentioned prostration (al-kabb) first as an indication of its opposite, which is mentioned second, and He mentioned straightness second as an indication of crookedness, which is mentioned first. And the secret of it is that He mentioned the most painful of what befalls the criminal and the most comforting of what befalls the Muslim.

Since the Arabs addressed by this Reminder used to vie with one another in boasting about guidance along tangible paths, and in never failing to acknowledge a kindness, however small, from its giver, He first negated this from them by establishing proofs of their gross error in everything in which they opposed the Messenger (ﷺ), regarding the immaterial path they had taken as their religion. Since that path is more noble than the tangible one, He followed it with a statement of their detachment from [the second, together with emphasis on their detachment from] the first. He said, commanding the Messenger (ﷺ) to alert them, since a human is most receptive to his own kind, for he is most inclined toward it, (p-259) removing them from the rank of understanding God, glorified and exalted be He, because of the lowliness of their aspirations and the shortness of their vision, although He had granted them a share of presence by qualifying them to address the Messenger (ﷺ), since they were established in what is mentioned in the verse, through which knowledge is hoped for and discernment and understanding are inherited: ﴿Say﴾, i.e., O most noble of creation and most compassionate toward them, reminding them of what sovereignty (al-mulk) removed from them of corrupting factors and gathered for them of beneficial things, of powers and intellect, so that they would return to Him and not rely in any state upon anyone but Him, and so that they would reflect on His subtle craftsmanship and good nurture, whereby each of them walks upright. ﴿He﴾, i.e., God, glorified and exalted be He, ﴿is the One who﴾ honored you with this Reminder and clarified this clarification for you, He alone, ﴿who brought you into being﴾, i.e., originated you and raised you through the stages of nurture, as He developed you through the phases of creation in the womb, and made easy for you, after your emergence, soft (digestible) food, since the stomach was too weak for anything denser.

Since among the greatest of the magnificent blessings after existence is the intellect, he followed it with that, [and began] with the means of alerting them, and said: ﴿And He made for you﴾, i.e., specifically, as a consequence of the body He created, ﴿hearing﴾ [i.e. complete hearing], ﴿so that you might hear﴾ (p-260) what your hearts comprehend, so that it guides you. He made it singular because of the slight variation in it, so that the secret of His disposing of hearts might appear in its utmost diversity, though it is the greatest of the paths conveying meanings to them. ﴿And sight﴾, so that you might look upon His works, take heed, and restrain yourselves from what would ruin you. ﴿And hearts﴾, i.e., the minds that He made in utmost intensity of perception for what the rest of the animals do not perceive, ﴿so that you might reflect and thus turn toward what exalts you﴾. It was made plural because of the great variation in the light of sight and in the grasp of thoughts. This is an alert to the perfection of these faculties in grasping realities through the refinement of the inner secret for the precision of thought. Shaykh Wali al-Din al-Malawi said: Look at the hearts, how they judge that two is more than one, that one body cannot be in two places at one time, that two opposites cannot combine, and other things that are not hidden.

Since the intended sense was: "So you walked like one who is prone upon his face, and did not use any of these noble faculties for what they were created," its rendering was ﴿little﴾, and he emphasized the meaning with what gives the form of a negation, saying ﴿what﴾. Since the soul's longing for the agent of the description of the verbal noun increased, He indicated it, glorified and exalted be He, by His saying (p-261) ﴿you give thanks﴾, i.e., you bestow thanks upon the One who gave you what you do not value at its worth, by using it for what it was created for, while you claim to be the most thankful of people for kindness and the most knowing of them in recognition.

When God (glorified is He) pointed out their distance from guidance and from gratitude, the two qualities by which they all boast over people, and sought to win them over through the subtle divine and spiritual faculties He had placed in them, which by their luminous nature call them to ascend to the abodes of holiness and the mines of intimacy, He pointed to His power to gather them (to the Resurrection). This was a warning to them against persisting in turning away, through a meaning that each of them finds within himself, in a manner that indicates the perfection of His power, by what He placed in them together with those subtle faculties, along with the dense natures of earth which necessitate descent. So that he, when those subtle faculties raise him up through repentance, may strive to purify the traces of those dense, lowly natures, just as the crop, when it is harvested, is left with remnants of those roots, which, if they are not uprooted from their origin, return the plant to what the crop was at first. Then He said, resuming as an explanation, since this is a self-sufficient proof whose sufficiency for what came before is already established:

﴿Say: He﴾, that is, He alone, ﴿is the One who created you﴾, that is, brought you into being, scattered you, spread you, multiplied you and produced you after you were like specks, weak children. Then He strengthened you, then He made you grey-haired and weak, and He lodged in you anger, dread and obstinacy, which drive you to crave what the stirring natures incline you toward, ﴿on the earth﴾, which was previously stated that He made it subservient to you and provided you from it with plants, whose emergence from it was previously mentioned (p. 262), then His returning it to it, its perishing within it, then its restoration as it was after it had become dust and a crumbling, dead thing, is a proof of the power to resurrect, with no difference in that between Him and you at all. Thus the beginning came from Him, ﴿and to Him﴾ alone ﴿you will be gathered﴾, gradually at first to the barzakh (the intermediate realm between death and resurrection) [and -] and all at once on the Day of Resurrection, in the easiest manner, with whomever of His servants He wills, against your will, as your affair was in the world, for none of you has loved anything more than ease and rest. So it is as if He (glorified is He) compels him through the opposing natures He placed in him, and stirs up for him the means to seek his sustenance and other affairs, to strive toward what he dislikes. Just as He had power over that for you at the beginning, He has power over its like at the end, so that He may judge among you and recompense each for his deeds, as every king does with his subjects, and every person among you with his community.

The implied sense is: "Indeed, He, glory be to Him, made His admonition of them complete, through Himself and upon your tongue, O most noble of creation (ﷺ)." The context definitively indicates this. Having said that, he mentioned their state at that point, to inform (us) of the thickness of their natures, since their inner secrets were not refined to accept the love of God Most High, nor to stir up the good states of steadfast patience, certainty, a good disposition to accept admonitions, fear, and not taking pride in anyone other than God Most High, whether in terms of benefit or harm. Likewise, he turned the speech away from them (to the third person), as an indication of intense anger toward them: ﴿They say﴾, i.e., they renew this saying continuously, as mockery and denial. It is permissible that it be a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the waw in "[bal - ] lajjū" (rather, they persisted): ﴿When is this?﴾ They increased the mockery by saying ﴿the promise﴾, and they incited and agitated, making the denial clear [according to their claim] by saying: ﴿if you are﴾ truthful by nature and disposition ﴿truthful﴾ in that there is no escape for us from it, and that you are brought near to God. For if they had possessed the firmness of patience and certainty, they would not have been so reckless as to utter this ugly saying, whose outward form is a request for information about the time of the threatened matter, and whose inner meaning is hastening it in mockery and denial.

When their saying this was combined with their hurrying the matter of the Hour, belittling it to the point that, in their view, it was as though it were before the promised good, and it implied that the Hour is among the things that creatures could know the exact time of, He negated that, explaining its greatness by the greatness of its affair being in His hand. So He said, commanding him to answer them, and indicating that such turning away is unnecessary, because they do not deny His knowledge, which is exalted, in that denial: ﴿Say﴾, O most noble of creation, alerting them to attain certainty that what they know and judge by their knowledge, and what they cannot know they should refer to God: ﴿Knowledge is only﴾, that is, the all-encompassing knowledge from every aspect, of what you asked about, such as determining the time of this promise and other things. And in order to show the excellence of knowledge, which follows from the perfection of His complete power, He turned the speech away from the generality of mercy to conveying absolute generality through the greatest Name, so it was said: ﴿with God﴾, that is, the One who has encompassing knowledge of all the attributes of perfection. He is the one with whom, and in whose hand, is everything that is willed from Him. No one else has knowledge of it, and His awe prevents the world, with its greatness, from daring to ask Him about what He has not permitted. His majesty requires the singling out of great matters, and His exalted saying alludes to this: ﴿And I am only﴾. Since the context is one of frightening and warning, and warning is sufficient with the mere possibility of the threatened event occurring, how much more so when it is probable, and how much more when it is known to occur in general, so that the sensible person is always expecting it, He said: ﴿a warner﴾, that is, perfect in the matter of warning, which necessarily entails good news for whoever obeys the warnings. I have no role with this Mighty King other than that, so I have no access to asking Him about what He does not permit me to ask about.

Since the warner may not be able to establish proof for what he warns about, because for the sensible person acceptance requires only a strong presumption of his truthfulness, or even the possibility of his truthfulness, in guarding against what he warns of, [p. 265] He clarified that this is not the case, saying: ﴿clear﴾, that is, one who makes the warned matter fully manifest by establishing proofs for it, until it becomes as though it were witnessed by one who is receptive to knowledge.

The passage opens with the phrase "Since what he warns of must certainly come to pass, and everything that is coming is near, he expressed this with the particle *fa'* and the past tense, turning the minds toward the reality of disgrace, since the moment of seeing the punishment is most fitting for humiliation:" ﴿So when they see it﴾, meaning the promise, through the unveiling of what was promised, at the moment of its occurrence. He established the meaning of the past tense. The *fa'* is connected with his words ﴿near﴾, meaning close to them, very near. This is expressed by using the verbal noun (*masdar*, the verbal noun form) in place of the active participle (*ism al-fa'il*, the active participle), for the sake of emphasizing the intended meaning. He reinforced the intensity with the *ta'* (the feminine ending), because it is used for intensification when the feminine sense is not intended, especially if another indication points to that. [ with the *ta'*, because it occurs for intensification - ]

Since the warning in the case of the warner is the occurrence of evil, without restriction to its coming from a specific source, he said ﴿will be evil﴾. Since evil appears on the face, he said ﴿faces﴾. He used the explicit noun in place of a pronoun, for generality and to attach the judgment to the description, saying ﴿of those who disbelieved﴾. Meaning: the evil and extreme abhorrence will appear on the faces of those who brought about this description, even at the lowest degree of bringing it about, and its cause is grief.

Since there is nothing more painful than reproach when the hated thing encompasses them without any need to specify its agent, he used the passive form in his words ﴿and it will be said﴾, meaning to them, as rebuke and reproof: ﴿This is what﴾, meaning what has preceded of your obstinacy, your scheming and your arrogance (p. 266) ﴿you used to﴾, meaning by nature and disposition, ﴿call for﴾, meaning by it, because of it and on account of it. He turned the speech to address them directly, because rebuke by it is more painful in punishment: ﴿you used to call for﴾, meaning you sought and expected the seeking of it with intense seeking, reaching the utmost effort in it, in a manner of urgency, that its hated consequence might descend upon you, like one who does not care about it in any way. You repeat that seeking and return to it at every time, turning away from striving for deliverance from the assault of punishment and from attaining the good promise of abundant reward. This is to show the strength of their seeking and their eagerness for it, mocking it, until it is as if they had no object of seeking other than it. He placed first the prepositional phrase (*jarr*), which generally indicates exclusivity (*ikhtisas*), so this is the reflexive form (*ifti'al*, verbal form VIII) from "da'a al-shay' bi al-shay'" when one seeks it. "Da'a-hu Allah bi makruhin" means: He brought it down upon him with it.

(p-267) Since it is well known that whoever forbids another from his desires and insists on it will be hated by that forbidder, who wishes for his destruction, how much more so when the forbidder adds warning and intimidation with what his intellect cannot reach and whose premise he cannot see as certain. The unbelievers strove with every effort for the destruction of the Prophet ﷺ and those who followed him. The destruction of the warner benefits the one warned only on the assumption that he is saved from the terror of what the warner was warning him of. So Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to remind them of this, so that they would consider the threatened outcome. If it is possible, they should strive for deliverance from what may come upon them of punishment, and take in fleeing from it an easy and far path away from the evil of the outcome, and enter the wide refuge from it through the widest door. Or they should cease striving for the destruction of the warner and set aside the means they had prepared against him, so that, if he is truthful, he may guide them to something that protects them or lightens their calamity. Thus He said, alerting to the severity of caution against the plotting of Allah and to the absence of complacency about it for the believing obedient one, since he knows that he cannot measure Allah with His due measure, so how much less the disobedient, let alone the unbeliever. He repeats the command "Say" to alert that every sentence that comes with it suffices to indicate the purpose of the surah and returns to it, because of what it contains of manifest power and abundant greatness:

﴿Say﴾, that is, O best of all creation, most noble, greatest and most pious, to these people who have long been impatient with you while they wish for your destruction out of envy, blindness in their hearts, and distance and rejection, and for whom that decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing, has become firm and encircled them: ﴿Tell me﴾, that is, inform me of a matter about which you are certain in the sense of being as sure as sight.

Since they did not know the outcome of the matter regarding his destruction and that of those with him, by what they intend against them, He warned them of its consequence by using the particle of doubt, and by attributing the destruction to Allah, expressing the Name that indicates the utmost greatness to a degree that leaves nothing of it to anyone else, to inform them that, with certainty, nothing is in their hands, so He does not fear them in any way. So He said: ﴿If Allah destroys me﴾, that is, causes me to die by punishment or otherwise, ﴿Allah﴾, who possesses the attributes of majesty and generosity by which He protects His friend and breaks His enemy, ﴿and those with me﴾, that is, of the believers and helpers, may Allah be pleased with them all, with His anger upon us, along with what we possess of the means of obedience through righteous deeds, which He, glorified is He, has ordained as the cause of success and salvation, until no one remains who would trouble you by restraining you from the desire that leads to the appetites and by urging the intellect that guarantees salvation. ﴿Or He shows us mercy﴾ by victory and the manifestation of Islam, as we hope, so He saves us thereby from every evil, protects us from every feared thing, and grants us every joy. So the verse is of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which elements are omitted on each side that are supplied by the other): it mentioned destruction first as an indication of deliverance second, and mercy second as an indication of anger first. ﴿Then who﴾ — and the apparent state would require: "will protect you," given your seeking the means of success and salvation without means, but rather with means that contradict salvation and bring punishment. So He placed the apparent noun in place of the pronoun, generalizing and tying the ruling to the attribute, and as an appeal to them to accept faith and return from disbelief. So He said: ﴿will protect the disbelievers﴾, that is, the two groups in disbelief, by warding off from them what a neighbor wards off from his neighbor, ﴿from a painful punishment﴾ that He will inflict upon them, by which they know that nothing [except] is in His hand. Otherwise, someone would be saved from death, which He created and decreed among His servants as recompense for what they used to distress those who called them to Him and advised them. So if nothing can save them from His punishment, whether we die or survive, then what befits them, if they are intelligent, is to strive for what delivers them from His punishment, not to strive for the destruction of one who is striving for their deliverance from the punishment. They cannot destroy him at all except by the decree of the One who commanded him to warn them.

When al-Biqa'i's commentary says that one cannot generalize with blessing except one who has all-encompassing power, blessing and mercy, and that reminding of blessings is more effective in winning sympathy, he turned the speech toward an expression that is explicit in this regard. So he said, reminding them of this because they know that there is no blessing upon them except from Him, and they acknowledge this, so that they fear Him and remember the generality of His power, and thus they would know His power over resurrection, and the dispute would be settled: ﴿Say﴾, O best of creation: ﴿He﴾, that is, Allah alone, ﴿is the Most Merciful (al-Rahman)﴾, that is, the One whose mercy encompasses everything that Lordship embraces. It does not befit the intellect of any sensible person that He would leave any of His creatures under the oppression of his oppressor without taking their right for them, because even the least of people would not accept that for himself while being powerless, so how about one who is of complete power? Otherwise He would not have been able to have universal mercy. ﴿We have believed in Him﴾ (p-270), that is, I and whoever believes in me, by this decisive proof that nothing is comparable to Him, so it is sufficient in faith in Him. ﴿And upon Him﴾, that is, Him alone, ﴿we have relied﴾, because nothing is in the hand of anyone else; otherwise He would show mercy to whom He wants to punish, or punish whom He wants to show mercy. So whatever occurs at the hands of His creatures, whether mercy or retribution, it is He who causes it, because He is the Doer in essence, possessing all the attributes that befit Him. So we hope for His good and fear none other than Him. We have affirmed to Him, through this expression, His exclusive divinity and lordship, so we shall not, in our journey toward Him, require any hindrance from remembering Him and reflecting on His favors, even if that hindrance is precious in the apparent life of this world, and even if it is frightening, for there is no fear with Him, glory be to Him. Thus reliance upon Him is deliverance from every destruction and a means of attaining every virtue. He did not act as you act in your reliance upon your men, your status, and your wealth.

When this has made clear the path of correctness and dispelled every doubt, and there was necessarily a return to Him and a turning back, to complete mercy through reward and punishment, He based on it His saying: ﴿So you will know﴾, that is, when He manifests Himself to you with the attribute of subjugation before long, by a promise that will not be broken, ﴿who it is﴾, that is, of us and of you, who is ﴿in manifest error﴾ (p-271), that is, who is in a course not leading to a goal, surrounded by error such that he has no power to disengage from it unless he obeys one who pulls him by the hand and brings him out of it. And since a thing that has some ambiguity in it might perhaps call for accepting an excuse, He said: ﴿manifest﴾, that is, clear in itself, making it plain to everyone that there is no concealment in it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 67, verse 30:

When He, glorified be He, opened the surah with the great blessing of His, the perfection of His power, and His singularity in His dominion, and indicated this by His singularity in causing death and giving life, He concluded with the like of that, with water, whose existence is the cause of life and whose absence is the cause of death. So He said, striking with the warning, indicating by the repetition of the command an increase in rebuke, reproach and reprimand, showing the specification of what was left vague concerning the people of misguidance, and expressly stating what He had alluded to of that generality.

﴿Say﴾ meaning: O greatest of Our creation and the most knowing of Us. ﴿Tell me﴾ meaning: inform me with information free of confusion and obscurity. Since he (ﷺ) was intensely concerned for this noble Prophet, his heart was calmed regarding their threats by an indication of gentleness toward them for his sake. So He began the threat with the particle of doubt, saying: ﴿if﴾. And since a blessing is at its greatest when it is in the morning, which is the time when deliverance is awaited, He said: ﴿your water becomes[ ] ﴾, meaning that which you count as in your hands, by what the possessive construction indicated.

Since the intended purpose is emphasis, He made it the verbal noun itself, saying: ﴿gone down﴾, meaning: sinking into the earth in such a way that it is not possible for you to reach it by any kind of stratagem, by what the description with the verbal noun indicates. ﴿Then who will bring you﴾ while you are weak then, needy, your hearts unhinged and your thoughts confused, ﴿flowing water﴾, meaning: flowing constantly without cutting off, or manifest to the eyes, easy to obtain, ﴿except Allah, the Lord of the worlds﴾, for He is the One Able to do that. Thus that other (i.e., the second) has returned, as you see, to that first, and embraced it in the best and most complete manner. And Allah knows best.
